lessons.title: Establish the bench and read cluster health
topics: Establish the bench and read cluster health
lessons.body:
For the login step, use your own API address. If the CLI cannot open a browser in the guest, use the private login instructions from your cluster console and continue at `oc whoami`.

Select **Open practice terminal** in the desktop reader and select **Client**. This course uses the shared AlmaLinux 10.3 kit. Use the starter manifests in this course’s references. For cluster exercises, use the OpenShift console’s **Command Line Tools** page to obtain the matching oc client and install it on this guest. Connect to your assigned practice cluster from the client using your private login session. Helm and optional Operators are required only for the lessons that use them. The AlmaLinux pair supplies the terminal. The cluster owner supplies the API, permissions and any registry or storage services.

A team reports “the cluster is down.” You can still log in. Either observation could be true for a particular user or application. Begin by narrowing the claim. The console shows a human-oriented view of the same API objects that oc reads. A Deployment belongs to a namespace. A Node and a ClusterOperator belong to the cluster. A healthy API can describe an application that is failing.

## Trace one observation
Open the Administrator console, locate the cluster overview and record the current project. In a terminal use the lab contract’s identity checks. In your assigned practice cluster, create `os-shift` or select the project provisioned for you. Inspect the release, operator conditions, nodes and project events as your identity permits. A project user receiving Forbidden on nodes has learned something about access. Ask the cluster operator for a scoped health observation before claiming node failure.

On the workstation, create the named project only when it has not been provisioned and your practice identity can create projects.

*Transcript lines 1–12.*

If the owner already created os-shift, select it instead.

*Transcript lines 13–14.*

Inspect with your current identity. Cluster-wide reads may return Forbidden to a project-only account.

*Transcript lines 15–26.*

Use API discovery and the Deployment field schema to identify a field before editing it. Find a running Deployment in the console, open its YAML and compare its UID with a terminal read in the same project. Once it exists, notice from the kit is suitable. A health handoff includes time, identity, project, UID and the smallest affected surface. For lifecycle practice create a second empty scratch project using a unique name, inspect its UID, delete only that project and observe its disappearance. A pending deletion may be waiting for finalizers.

lessons.title: Read a rollout from spec to running bytes
topics: Read a rollout from spec to running bytes
lessons.body:
A Deployment describes how many copies of a pod template belong in this release. Its controller manages ReplicaSets. A ReplicaSet maintains pods. A Service selects matching pods independently. A ready pod can therefore belong to a healthy rollout while its service selects nothing.

Apply the base in the practice service reference. Inspect the Deployment, its ReplicaSets and the pods selected by the application label. A request for two replicas, two available replicas and two ready endpoints should agree once rollout completes. Read one pod’s actual `status.containerStatuses[0].imageID` and compare it with the tag in the pod template. A tag can move. The digest identifies particular content, with platform-specific manifests possible. Use the registry image information for the authorized reference to inspect its platform and digest.

After deploying the blue kit in the current practice project.

*Transcript lines 1–19.*

Assign POD to a displayed pod name and IMAGE to the authorized image reference. The pull spec can be a tag while the running image ID contains a digest.

*Transcript lines 20–25.*

Introduce a reversible fault by changing only the service selector in your working copy to `app: bulletin`. Apply and repeat the checks. A normal rollout beside an EndpointSlice with no ready addresses points to selection. Inspect the pod labels, restore the intended selector, then run the controlled client request. For a failing process inspect pod state, current logs and the previous container log when a prior instance exists. Pending scheduling, a failed image pull, a restarted process and an unready HTTP path leave different evidence. Export the live Deployment into a scratch file to inspect controller-added identity, status and defaults. Keep the original declarative source as the portable version.

For a failing practice pod, assign POD to its name. Inspect the current state and log for that pod.

*Transcript lines 26–32.*

If the same container restarted in this pod, inspect its prior instance separately.

lessons.title: Render overlays, templates and Helm releases
topics: Render overlays, templates and Helm releases
lessons.body:
The green shift needs three replicas and a different page. Copying the whole blue Deployment would let fixes diverge. A Kustomize overlay applies differences to a common base. A Template substitutes declared inputs into objects. Helm renders a chart and can track a named release across upgrades.

Build the three fixtures in Portable render inputs. Save their rendered YAML and identify the ConfigMap bytes, Deployment replica count and target namespace. Begin in the kit directory with the blue base running in os-shift and the approved probe from the practice service kit ready there. Compare the live objects with the green overlay.

*Transcript lines 1–7.*

Review the diff before applying it. Mounted ConfigMap changes propagate asynchronously. Repeat the HTTP check until the green content converges within the lab’s timeout. An environment variable sourced from a ConfigMap requires a replacement process.

*Transcript lines 8–15.*

In the same project, process the amber Template. Check the resulting ConfigMap independently.

*Transcript lines 16–19.*

Before extending the chart in Packaged service, use the marker-only chart in os-shift. Record the green revision and compare the release values with the live ConfigMap.

lessons.title: Locate a failed request across route, service and pod
topics: Locate a failed request across route, service and pod
lessons.body:
Work outward from a known response. A Route associates a host with a Service. The Service maps a named or numeric port to an application port. EndpointSlices reveal whether the selected backends are ready. A 503 from the router proves a response came back from an ingress path. It does not identify which backend component failed.

In the blue project, fetch the page from a probe. Publish an edge route for the Service’s web port with HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection and read the assigned host. Use the cluster’s trusted CA to check the HTTPS status and exact page from a separate client. Supply the trusted CA file when the router uses a private CA. Check HTTP redirection separately. Inspect the router-specific admitted condition in the Route status. Diagnose a broken service selector without replacing a working certificate.

In the blue project before a route of this name exists.

*Transcript lines 1–4.*

On the separate HTTPS client, set HOST to the returned hostname and CA to the trusted router CA file.

*Transcript lines 5–9.*

In the blue project.

*Transcript lines 10–17.*

At edge termination TLS ends at the router. Re-encrypt establishes another TLS session to a TLS-capable backend and requires the destination CA to be trusted by the router. Passthrough routes use the client’s SNI and leave TLS termination at the backend. In a second project use the owner’s HTTPS test backend and CA to build a re-encrypt route to the named TLS Service port with the destination CA. Verify a good response and explain the failure with the wrong test CA. For a raw TCP service with no HTTP or TLS/SNI, use an owner-approved LoadBalancer Service where an implementation exists. Check its assigned address and a real protocol exchange. A pending external address can indicate that the infrastructure did not allocate a load balancer.

In the separate approved project with a TLS-capable backend. Set ROUTE_NAME, SERVICE, HTTPS_PORT and CAFILE to its actual route name, service, port and trusted backend CA file.

*Transcript lines 18–19.*

lessons.title: Prove one allowed client and one denied client
topics: Prove one allowed client and one denied client
lessons.body:
A namespace boundary alone does not express which pods may connect. An ingress NetworkPolicy selecting the server pods isolates their ingress. Allowed traffic is the union of matching policies. Before introducing a policy, run the same baseline request from both practice client pods. If one already fails, fix that condition before using denial as evidence.

Before applying the readers policy, use two ready probes in the blue project. Resolve any failed baseline request first.

*Transcript lines 1–4.*

Save this policy as `readers.yaml` in the kit directory. Both clients reside in the same namespace; a pod selector alone in a peer selects from that namespace.

*Transcript lines 5–17.*

*Transcript lines 18–19.*

Issue fresh requests from both clients after policy convergence. Expect the approved client to retrieve blue and the guest to fail within its timeout. Confirm both can still resolve the service name. This rule can also remove router ingress to the selected pods. For a desired external route, add a separate allowance for the actual ingress topology using the cluster’s supported ingress namespace labels and documented source behavior. Test both the external HTTPS path and client isolation again.

After the readers policy has converged, repeat from each client in os-shift. The approved request should succeed and the guest should fail.

*Transcript lines 20–24.*

For a default OVN-Kubernetes bench whose router traffic is identified by the documented ingress namespace label, apply this second policy beside readers. Identify the actual ingress endpoint publishing strategy with the owner before adapting it. For host-networked routers, verify the plugin’s host-origin handling with the owner and test the observed source. A permission for every host-networked workload or a whole node subnet would expand the trusted surface.

*Transcript lines 25–38.*

A namespace selector and pod selector in the same peer are combined; two separate peers allow either. Demonstrate this distinction using a second course project with a labeled probe. Preserve only the intended allowance, then clean up the test policy before the next independent exercise.

lessons.title: Budget a tenant and produce bounded batch work
topics: Budget a tenant and produce bounded batch work
lessons.body:
Suppose the pod count quota is five and four pods already exist. A Deployment requesting two more replicas may be accepted even though only one further pod can be admitted. The replica controller reports the blocked creation. The admission failure and a scheduling failure occur at different points. Read the ReplicaSet events before changing node capacity.

Use a fresh project with room for experiments. Create a LimitRange with default CPU and memory requests and limits for containers, then a ResourceQuota counting pods and constraining summed requests. For a quick boundary test, limit the project to three pods and apply the base service, which uses two. Create a one-time Job that adds two and three. Wait for its Complete condition and read the result. Adjust the quota or remove finished practice jobs by name between trials. Inspect current quota usage before creating another workload.

In the fresh assigned project, before applying the two-pod base.

*Transcript lines 1–2.*

After the base pods are ready and the quota has space for the Job pod.

*Transcript lines 3–14.*

Create a CronJob that writes tick every quarter-hour. Start a named manual Job from the CronJob template. Verify its log. The manual Job can also carry a CronJob owner reference. For the scheduled run compare that owner UID with the CronJob UID, the controller-created Job annotation batch.kubernetes.io/cronjob-scheduled-timestamp with the matching schedule interval and CronJob status.lastScheduleTime, and the absence of cronjob.kubernetes.io/instantiate=manual. A completed manual Job only proves the template. In a disposable admin cluster compare project quotas with a ClusterResourceQuota whose selector matches only two practice projects. Show that using the shared allowance in one changes what the other can request.

When the assigned namespace has available quota.

*Transcript lines 15–22.*

lessons.title: Separate identity, permission and workload admission
topics: Separate identity, permission and workload admission
lessons.body:
A team lead can authenticate yet receive Forbidden when listing pods. A controller may be permitted to create Deployments while the resulting pod is rejected by a Security Context Constraint (SCC). Test the identity performing each operation. Use a separate credential for the test user and evaluate the exact verb, resource and namespace.

In the course project create service account reporter. Create a namespaced role granting get and list on pods and bind it to reporter. As an authorized administrator, check whether reporter may list pods, delete pods or read secrets. Confirm the positive result using a short-lived reporter credential in a separate protected kubeconfig, observing its expiration. Default token projection is unnecessary for the notice workload. Use a dummy value to practice creating and mounting a Secret, then confirm the application reads the file using a digest without printing the value. Base64 representation inside the API object does not protect disclosure.

As the os-shift project administrator. Create the reporter account only if the fresh fixture still needs it.

*Transcript lines 1–2.*

Once reporter exists, create the named role and binding in the fresh project.

*Transcript lines 3–6.*

As the lab administrator entitled to perform this impersonation check, with only the intended role granted.

*Transcript lines 7–12.*

For an approved specialized workload, compare its requested security context with ordinary restricted admission. On the owner's isolated fixture, inspect the authorized special-purpose service account and the admitted pod annotation `openshift.io/scc`. Run the supplied administrative diagnostic with that account, validate its limited purpose, and verify the ordinary course account cannot use that SCC. Privileged mode has substantial host access. Complete this comparison with the owner’s dedicated fixture and scoped binding. Record the least privilege that a normal notice pod actually needs.

lessons.title: Maintain project templates and an operator lifecycle
topics: Maintain project templates and an operator lifecycle
lessons.body:
A project template is a starting configuration for newly requested projects. It does not continuously reconcile every old project. Export the current Project cluster configuration and generate a lab copy of the bootstrap project template. Preserve its existing parameters, project creation and admin binding. Add a named LimitRange to the template’s object list, using the project parameter for its namespace. Store it as a uniquely named Template in openshift-config. On the dedicated bench, select that name in `project.config.openshift.io/cluster.spec.projectRequestTemplate.name`. Request a fresh project as the test developer and compare the new defaults with an existing project. Restore the original named reference or the previous unset state.

As the dedicated bench administrator, save the starting template in a new local file.

*Transcript lines 1–2.*

An operator adds or watches resource types and acts on custom resources. Under classic OLM a Subscription selects a package, channel, catalog and update approval strategy. An InstallPlan resolves dependencies; a ClusterServiceVersion reports the installed operator state. Installing an operator and creating an instance of its API are different steps. In OperatorHub inspect the lab owner’s approved harmless package, compatible install modes, namespace and channel. Install it using manual approval. Inspect the proposed InstallPlan, approve the expected change, then observe the CSV in Succeeded and the new type in API discovery. Apply the provider’s small sample instance, read its status and verify its stated effect.

Supply OPERATOR_NS with the actual approved installation namespace; inspect the installed API only after the approved OLM installation.

*Transcript lines 3–11.*

For teardown inventory the operator’s instances and any data they own. Remove only the practice instance through its supported process and wait for finalizers. Remove the Subscription and installed CSV per the operator’s instructions, then check residual CRDs, secrets and storage separately. A missing Subscription alone cannot prove that a workload or its data was deleted.

lessons.title: Stage A practical — hand off a governed bulletin
topics: Stage A practical — hand off a governed bulletin
lessons.body:
Two shifts will share an application called bulletin. In a fresh practice project, deliver the text `edition=copper` on a trusted HTTPS route, with two available replicas and an independently rendered release marker. A viewer group may inspect pods and must fail to create workloads. An approved client may read the service; a second internal client may resolve it but must fail to retrieve it. lessons.title: Change identity providers without losing the recovery session
topics: Change identity providers without losing the recovery session
lessons.body:
The platform authenticates users against configured providers and maps the successful identity to an OpenShift User. A group role binding controls subsequent API authorization. When someone can log in but cannot list deployments, changing the identity provider first may break working access without fixing the binding.

On a disposable cluster configured for integrated OAuth, reserve an independent recovery credential. Work in a fresh private directory on the trusted administrator workstation. Keep the recovery session available while changing providers.

*Transcript lines 1–4.*

Inspect the existing provider names and mapping methods. Create a new password file for this bench only. Use the create option once. Adding users or changing an existing password uses the existing file.

*Transcript lines 5–12.*

Add an entry to the existing identityProviders array with a unique name, type `HTPasswd`, mappingMethod `claim` and `htpasswd.fileData.name` pointing at that Secret. Review the complete array before applying it. Wait for the authentication ClusterOperator to return to Available and test both users in separate sessions.

For LDAP, match a verified TLS CA, search base/filter, bind identity and referenced bind password Secret, and map a stable directory attribute to the user ID. For Keycloak OIDC, register the cluster-provided OAuth callback URL for the provider name in the lab client, configure the issuer URL, client ID, referenced client Secret and preferred-username claim, then test discovery, trust and mapping with one lab person. Add providers without replacing the earlier array. Change one input at a time. Preserve two known-working test logins and investigate an identity collision before assigning an existing account. Keep issuer certificates, directory-bind credentials and OAuth client secrets out of submissions.

During the documented removal exercise, verify that reader2 is the intended test identity. Remove its local entry and use the access reference to update the Secret.

*Transcript lines 13–14.*

Inspect the relationship between the test Identity and User before removing those objects. Invalidate sessions as required by the exercise, then verify that a fresh login with the removed account fails. Keep an independent working administrator session throughout.

topics: Reconcile group membership, including removals
lessons.body:
An LDAP identity provider can authenticate a person even when OpenShift group membership is stale. Group sync is a separate job with separate inputs. Decide which directory owns each group and which OpenShift group names it controls. A manually maintained group and a synchronized group with the same name can cause conflicting membership or ownership.

Use the Red Hat RFC2307 example from the authentication reference as a local `LDAPSyncConfig`. Adapt the server URL, CA and bind input, groups and users search bases and scope, UID/name attributes, and the group member attribute to your directory’s actual schema. An Active Directory nested-group configuration uses a different mapping. For this RFC2307 fixture groups have a unique cn within the search base. Put the exact test group CN in groups.txt, one per line (for example, night). Preview only that group before writing any changes. Use the posixGroup filter and explicit never alias dereferencing from the supplied group and user queries, with groupUIDAttribute set to cn. Read the proposed OpenShift group, directory identifier and all member names. After review, confirm the scoped sync and inspect the resulting group’s LDAP identity annotations. A role binding to that group should allow the target verb for a member and deny it for a nonmember; confirm with fresh credentials.

In the lab administrator session after configuring the unique RFC2307 test CN. Run the first command as a preview.

topics: Prove which credentials a kubeconfig is using
lessons.body:
A context is a tuple of cluster, user entry and optional namespace. The context name does not authenticate the caller. An API endpoint and certificate authority establish where the request goes. A client certificate plus private key, a service-account token, or an interactive OAuth token establishes a particular caller. Local context names can be reassuringly similar while pointing at different credentials.

Use an isolated file per test and a restrictive umask. Build a cluster entry for the supplied API and CA. Add the short-lived, owner-issued client certificate and matching key as the user entry. Create and select a context that pairs these entries and selects the practice namespace. Verify the server, authenticated subject, an allowed list and a forbidden write. Never paste a raw kubeconfig into the evidence record.

On the private workstation use a fresh owner-only file at CFG. Supply owner-approved API, CA, CERT and KEY paths/values for the issued test credential.

For the token trial, have the authorized administrator issue a short-lived reporter token directly to a private file as shown below. Use the lab’s private credential entry procedure and a second protected file to set an equivalent cluster/context with a token user. The actual token lifetime is determined by the server. Read the authenticated subject and compare its permissions with the certificate subject. In a timed lab, repeat using an expired test token and observe authentication failure. A fresh valid token without a role binding instead normally authenticates and receives an authorization denial for a protected resource. Demonstrate the distinction before requesting a replacement or adjusting permissions.

Switch to the authorized issuing administrator’s session, verify the selected server and identity, and issue the token directly to a temporary private file.

Use the lab’s private credential-entry procedure to configure the second protected kubeconfig. On the test workstation, set TOKEN_CFG to that file. With only the reporter-status reader binding from the tenancy exercise, confirm the service account’s identity and permissions.

*Transcript lines 23–28.*

lessons.title: Prepare a backup that contains application data
topics: Prepare a backup that contains application data
lessons.body:
A YAML export can recreate a PVC object while leaving every byte of the original volume missing. A container image tag can exist while pointing at different content. The backup contract for the archive service includes the Deployment, configuration, claim, application data and an image that the recovery cluster can pull. Write a unique record and compute its digest inside the mounted directory before backup. Store that digest separately. Quiesce the fixture writer or use the application’s supported consistency mechanism; a snapshot alone does not guarantee database transaction consistency.

Export the portable application source, excluding live metadata, credentials and status. Copy the full multi-platform image set from an authenticated test registry to a local OCI layout using the authorized reference and digest. Copy the saved layout to the designated recovery repository, inspect the resulting manifest/platform and perform an independent pull. Record the destination digest since a registry or format conversion can affect it. Grant the recovery namespace its own pull access.

Set SOURCE to the approved registry repository and DIGEST to its full digest (including sha256:). Use a fresh local archive-image directory.

Configure a DataProtectionApplication with the provider-specific backup location, credentials, plugins and CSI or file-data protection method using the documented example matching that installation. Wait for the DPA reconciled condition, a running Velero deployment and an Available BackupStorageLocation. For CSI, match the claim’s storage driver with a supported VolumeSnapshotClass and the Velero selection label shown in the official reference. Confirm snapshots are supported on this cluster. An on-array snapshot alone cannot satisfy a loss-of-array recovery requirement; choose a supported data mover or volume backup path where needed.

Create a scoped Velero Backup with `spec.includedNamespaces: [os-archive]` and the chosen storage/snapshot settings. Inspect the named Backup, its warnings and errors, the snapshot or data-transfer objects and the completion status. Schedule a recurring backup using a Velero Schedule with the reviewed template and a suitable UTC cron expression. Confirm a new backup carrying that schedule’s label and matching the schedule template. Completing the API resource is only the midpoint of acceptance.

topics: Roll a configuration to an identified worker pool
lessons.body:
A worker node label can make a machine a scheduling candidate. A MachineConfigPool (MCP) selects nodes and selects the configurations the Machine Config Operator renders for them. These are separate selectors. A MachineSet, when supported by the platform, describes machines to create; adding a MachineSet replica is a capacity change, not an update to a file on an existing worker.

Inventory node roles, names, current pool memberships and capacity. Read the pool conditions, worker pool details and worker-role labels. Choose two spare lab workers and one comparison worker approved by the owner. Use the official custom MCP example: select only `node-role.kubernetes.io/bulletin` in the node selector and select both `worker` and `bulletin` roles for MachineConfigs. Confirm active configuration matches the desired configuration and verify marker bytes on a target through the owner’s read-only node inspection. Confirm the comparison worker lacks the marker. PVC-backed services must survive a planned disruption within the agreed availability budget.

Explore one installed special-purpose operator such as Node Tuning Operator. Inspect its profile selection and target nodes before adapting a harmless owner-supplied profile. Compare the reported effective profile on one target and one exclusion. Roll back the named practice configuration using its source and wait for pool convergence before removing role labels. lessons.title: Separate admission, placement and voluntary disruption
topics: Separate admission, placement and voluntary disruption
lessons.body:
A dedicated pool needs two protections. A workload must select its intended nodes, and unrelated workloads must be kept off them. A matching toleration permits a placement under a taint. It does not direct the scheduler to that pool. Required node affinity or a selector supplies the positive constraint.

Identify the dedicated workers by label. In the lab add a distinct label `erudior.example/pool=bulletin` and the owner-approved taint `erudior.example/pool=bulletin:NoSchedule` only on those workers. For a three-replica practice workload, set `spec.template.spec.nodeSelector` to that label, add a matching Equal toleration for the taint and spread replicas by hostname using topology spread or pod anti-affinity consistent with available capacity. Inspect the assigned node for each pod. For a deliberate negative control, remove the toleration from a separate workload that still requires the dedicated label. Inspect FailedScheduling and confirm the existing taint, then restore the fixture. Changing a NoSchedule taint does not evict existing pods.

In the practice workload namespace, after applying the intended placement constraints.

During an approved single eviction observe another ready replica on an eligible worker and measure service continuity. Never infer host diversity from replica count alone.

lessons.title: Promote a release by reconciling a reviewed commit
topics: Promote a release by reconciling a reviewed commit
lessons.body:
An administrator directly changes a ConfigMap to green and sees it revert. One controller may now be enforcing an older source. Separate the Git target revision, rendered desired manifest, last applied revision, live value and application health. A Synced application can be unhealthy; a Healthy application can be OutOfSync. A rollout that serves the wrong edition is an application failure even when both flags look favorable.

Install the supported OpenShift GitOps operator through the reviewed operator lifecycle. In the dedicated GitOps instance, check the Application CRD, ArgoCD instance health and controller service account. Grant it access only to the practice namespace using the documented namespace management and instance role configuration. Create an AppProject with the specific repository and destination namespace/server. Use a read-only repository credential where required, an approved CA and separate application and platform projects. Use the instance’s RBAC to grant a test viewer read access and a release operator synchronization access. Verify both with their own sessions.

Commit the base and green overlay to the lab Git repository. Add an Argo CD Application with the repository URL, the practice branch or approved tag, `path: overlays/green`, and destination `server: https://kubernetes.default.svc` plus the target namespace. Start with manual sync. Inspect the proposed diff, sync, then compare `status.sync.revision`, green HTTP bytes and rollout status. Make a practice live edit, observe the difference, then reconcile from the reviewed commit. Compare with automated self-heal behavior on this fixture. Revert via a reviewed Git commit when you need rollback. Restrict cluster-scoped configuration such as an approved namespace label to a separately reviewed platform project and controller permission.

On the Git workstation in the reviewed checkout, set GITOPS_NS to the selected controller namespace. Compare with the exact Application name from the kit after sync.

*Transcript lines 1–4.*

For the promotion pipeline, use a project-scoped OpenShift Pipeline that checks out the proposed revision, renders the Kustomize overlay or Helm chart, validates the manifests and records the revision/result. A failed render must stop the promotion. Merge a tested change, let Argo watch it and compare the PipelineRun’s tested revision with the deployed revision. The exact Task/ClusterTask names depend on the installed catalog; use pinned tasks and a minimally scoped service account in the course namespace. A passing build alone proves nothing about a subsequent controller sync.

lessons.title: Follow an alert from expression to test receiver
topics: Follow an alert from expression to test receiver
lessons.body:
Users report occasional errors. An empty graph can mean the service is healthy, the query has no matching series, or scraping failed. First identify which answer the instrument can actually supply. In Observe → Metrics run `up` and inspect label names and time ranges. Compare a known target with a nonmatching selector. A zero is a sample value; an empty result has no series in the selected window.

On a lab with user-workload monitoring enabled, deploy the owner’s metrics sample and inspect the metrics text on its named port, Service labels, and ServiceMonitor selectors and endpoints. Query a metric with its exact namespace and job labels. Introduce a wrong ServiceMonitor port name and observe a scrape or discovery difference; restore it. For a reproducible operator drill use a namespaced PrometheusRule whose test expression is `vector(1)` and which uses a unique alert name, label `team=course`, and a one-minute `for` period. Check that the rule is loaded and transitions from pending to firing. Configure a route and test receiver using the cluster’s user-alerting setup. Demonstrate delivery using a unique time window and test name.

During scheduled maintenance, create a short silence matching the exact practice alert and namespace. Verify the alert remains firing while notifications are suppressed. Use another simultaneously active test alert as an exclusion. Expire the silence and check future delivery according to the route’s repeat interval. Remove the test rule and confirm resolution. For an actual latency issue compare resource pressure, restarts, ready endpoints and request error/time series before selecting a remedy. Reducing a firing metric by silencing its receiver leaves the underlying measurement intact.

lessons.title: Trace an event through Vector, Loki and an external sink
topics: Trace an event through Vector, Loki and an external sink
lessons.body:
Pod logs, Kubernetes Events and node journal records originate from different paths and have different lifetimes. A Kubernetes Event on the API is not automatically a permanent application log. A collector can be running while an output rejects every batch. Separate generation, collection, authorization, routing and retention.

Install compatible Loki and OpenShift Logging operators on the isolated observability bench. Using the provider’s 6.x example create a LokiStack with the lab’s object-store Secret reference, storage schema/date, storage class, supported sizing profile and OpenShift logging tenancy. Confirm component readiness. Configure short-term retention through the supported LokiStack limits, then record both the chosen retention and object-store lifecycle. Create a service account with collection privileges only for the required sources. In a `ClusterLogForwarder` from `observability.openshift.io/v1`, name that service account, define a `lokiStack` output pointing at the local stack and an independently authenticated test external output, then reference them in the appropriate pipeline. Use an application input scoped to the practice namespace for outbound logs; inspect the installed CRD and the correct TLS/Secret fields for your output type. A configured destination that no pipeline references receives no traffic.

Generate a unique URI such as `/shift-317` against the notice service; Python’s access log should include that path even for a 404. Record the timestamp, pod UID and response status. Follow the same marker in the pod log, Vector collector observations, the Loki application tenant and the external receiver. Use the console’s log query builder to select this namespace and pod, then filter the line by the marker. Compare with an excluded namespace marker at the external receiver. A “no result” needs a successful positive query over the same window and tenant.

Deploy the matching documented Event Router fixture in openshift-logging with its read-only events permissions. Its own pod emits infrastructure logs. Configure a separate, authorized infrastructure collection/input and route to the local Loki infrastructure tenant. Keep the external exercise limited to the named application namespace; do not forward all infrastructure logs to that sink. Cause a benign scheduling warning using the unschedulable practice workload. Read the API event, Event Router output and corresponding local infrastructure log. A record about a workload in the practice namespace is still emitted by the Event Router pod in openshift-logging. Use authorized infrastructure log views to inspect a node/service record separately. references.title: Choose an RHCE pathway
references.body:
## Choose a specialization

An operations team can put the same application in four different hands. The Linux administrator restores the host after a boot or storage failure. The automation engineer writes a play that brings many hosts back to the agreed state. The OpenShift administrator looks after the cluster and its tenants. The application developer builds the image, tests it and promotes the application. Choose the work you want to practice.

| Role and credential route | First stage | Engineer stage | Erudior practice |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Enterprise Linux | EX200, system administration | EX342, diagnostics and troubleshooting | Start with [Zero to RHCSA](https://app.erudior.com/rhcsa-rhel10-administration), then open [Enterprise Linux](https://app.erudior.com/rhce-enterprise-linux). |
| Ansible | EX200, system administration | EX294, advanced Ansible administration | Start with [Zero to RHCSA](https://app.erudior.com/rhcsa-rhel10-administration), then open [Ansible on AlmaLinux 10](https://app.erudior.com/rhce-in-ansible-on-almalinux-10). |
| OpenShift | EX280, cluster administration | EX380, advanced cluster administration | [OpenShift administration](https://app.erudior.com/rhce-openshift-administration) contains both stages. |
| Cloud-native applications | EX188, container development | EX288, advanced OpenShift application development | [Cloud-native applications](https://app.erudior.com/rhce-cloud-native-applications) contains both stages. |

The two Linux-based routes share EX200. An OpenShift application developer and an OpenShift cluster administrator use the same platform but prepare for different exam pairs. Each Erudior practical is an original learning exercise. Red Hat awards credentials through its own examinations.

As of November 23, 2026, Red Hat also lists the AI developer credential, EX267. Its public catalog lists no engineer-level exam for AI. Check [Red Hat’s certification requirements](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/certifications?type=role) for updates or a particular exam version before registering.

references.title: Lab contract, scope and evidence
references.body:
Select **Open practice terminal** in the desktop reader and select **Client**. This course uses the shared AlmaLinux 10.3 kit. Use the starter manifests in this course’s references. For cluster exercises, use the OpenShift console’s **Command Line Tools** page to obtain the matching oc client and install it on this guest. Connect to your assigned practice cluster from the client using your private login session. Helm and optional Operators are required only for the lessons that use them. The AlmaLinux pair supplies the terminal. The cluster owner supplies the API, permissions and any registry or storage services.

Begin with shell navigation, reading YAML and a working understanding of containers, Linux files and TCP. Administrators who can work on a host will learn to follow a request from the OpenShift console through a controller, a pod, a service and an external router. The two stages prepare for EX280 and EX380, which Red Hat lists together for the RHCE in OpenShift. Both public exam pages name OCP 4.22 at the November 23, 2026 comparison. Erudior assignments are original practice. A passing course grade records Erudior work.

**Project bench.** Install a matching oc client, Helm 3, Git, curl and a YAML editor. Use a disposable OpenShift cluster with a working wildcard apps domain, trusted router CA, registry access and normal restricted security defaults. Ask the owner for a project creator or pre-created practice namespaces, a project administrator and a second test identity with limited access. Use separate local kubeconfig contexts to verify that each identity sees only its intended objects. Keep an administrator recovery session outside any identity-provider exercise. Project-only sandboxes support the namespaced labs your account can perform.

**Platform bench.** Use a dedicated resettable cluster. For placement, use at least two spare schedulable workers plus capacity outside the pair. Obtain explicit lab-admin access, a dedicated LDAP directory and OIDC lab client with trusted CAs, a private writable Git repository, a harmless operator listed in your catalog and sample CRs, user-workload monitoring and a test alert receiver. The recovery bench requires a supported OADP installation, compatible CSI driver and snapshot class, object storage and a test image registry reachable with the supplied trust chain. The logging bench requires compatible OpenShift Logging and Loki operators, object storage for Loki, a test external collector and a supported Event Router image. Match add-on versions to the cluster’s supported operator channels. Infrastructure-dependent fields are named as inputs in the exercises. Public sandbox access alone does not supply this bench.

**Cluster identity.** At the beginning of each session record the authenticated subject, API server, context, active project and OpenShift server version. Replace only the named course resources. Before using a cluster-scoped change export the current desired configuration into a protected local file, have the lab owner accept the proposed diff and agree on how the owner will restore it. Return the practice cluster to its baseline between stage finals. Credentials stay in the environment.

At the start of each session on the workstation, select the intended practice credentials first.

references.title: Practice service and controlled probes
references.body:
Save the following as `base/notice.yaml`. Create an empty directory named `base` first. The Python image runs a tiny read-only HTTP service from projected text, using a nonprivileged port. The registry tag is a convenient lab default. Where a mirror or registry policy requires it, replace this image with the authorized digest of the same Python runtime. A new project has its own UID range. Kubelet checks readiness at the pod address. The startup script tests whether this network namespace can bind an IPv6 wildcard. If it can, Python 3.12’s HTTP server binds `::` and requests IPv4-mapped connections where supported. Otherwise it binds `0.0.0.0`. This lets the same service accept the probe on IPv6-only, dual-stack and IPv4-only Linux benches. Diagnose a Running but unready pod by comparing its IP families with the listening address and reading readiness events.

*Transcript lines 1–59.*

Save separately as `base/kustomization.yaml`. Run commands from the directory containing `base`.

*Transcript lines 60–67.*

From the kit root, select the intended practice project. Apply the base, wait for rollout and inspect endpoint readiness and backend ports.

*Transcript lines 68–84.*

Create two short-lived diagnostic pods with distinct labels in the same project. Use the owner-approved Python image. Before adding a restrictive quota or network policy, check that both clients can reach the Service. If quota policies are already in effect, the probe manifests must satisfy their resource requests.

*Transcript lines 85–97.*

Both clients should read `edition=blue`. Keep them for the next exercises. Each probe exits after one hour. When replacing expired probes or when you finish, delete just the named pods in their project. To resume, create them again, wait for readiness and reestablish both baseline reads.

*Transcript lines 98–100.*
